gates.says: all 4 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-car-rental: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-car-rental: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-car-rental: 4.2: an approved 0100 places a hold and the money moves later when the acquirer clears, and the fuel-pump case shows a completion advice carrying the final amount while the rest is released.
recorded.prompt:q-after-the-outage: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-after-the-outage: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-after-the-outage: 4.1 shows setResponseMTI turning 0421 into 0430, and 4.3.1 says an issuer down for the 0420 sees only 0421s, which the fixed dispatcher answers with 0430.
recorded.prompt:q-no-answer: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-no-answer: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-no-answer: 4.4: a request without an answer is reversed, the reversal changes nothing if the purchase was not approved and gives the money back if it was, and it is a new message with its own STAN.
recorded.prompt:q-unanswered-echo: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-unanswered-echo: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-unanswered-echo: 4.2: an 0800 touches no account, and an echo with no answer needs no clean-up because it committed nothing; the next one is a new message.

recorded.prompt:q-car-rental:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-car-rental:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-car-rental:b: 4.2: an approved 0100 places a hold on the amount and the money moves later, so it does not move the 400.00 at once.
recorded.prompt:q-car-rental:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-car-rental:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-car-rental:c: 4.2: an approved 0200 posts the debit at once, so it is not a hold.
recorded.prompt:q-car-rental:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-car-rental:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-car-rental:d: 4.2: the fuel-pump case shows an 0200 debiting the full amount at once and the cardholder overpaying until a second message gives the difference back, so the account is not right and a further message is needed (partly true: an 0200 does post at once).
recorded.prompt:q-after-the-outage:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-after-the-outage:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-after-the-outage:b: 4.1: the fourth digit loses its repeat mark because the answer is to the message, not to one attempt, so 0421 -> 0430, never 0431.
recorded.prompt:q-after-the-outage:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-after-the-outage:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-after-the-outage:c: 4.3.1: if the issuer was down for the 0420, every attempt it sees is an 0421, and ignoring them means the reversal is never applied and the cardholder pays.
recorded.prompt:q-after-the-outage:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-after-the-outage:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-after-the-outage:d: 4.3 and 4.3.1: the sender keeps sending the advice as a repeat (fourth digit 1) until acknowledged, then parks it at its limit; it does not go back to an 0420.
recorded.prompt:q-no-answer:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-no-answer:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-no-answer:a: 4.4: sending the 0200 again makes a second purchase if the first was approved, so the cardholder pays twice.
recorded.prompt:q-no-answer:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-no-answer:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-no-answer:b: 4.4 says the unanswered request is never sent again because a resent 0200 is a second purchase, and 4.3 notes a new STAN makes a message look like a new transaction rather than a repeat.
recorded.prompt:q-no-answer:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-no-answer:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-no-answer:d: 4.4: the reversal has its own STAN and the issuer finds the original through field 90, not field 11 (partly true: the 'Networks differ' note says some networks want the original's STAN in field 11, but the page's rule refutes the option as stated).
recorded.prompt:q-unanswered-echo:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-unanswered-echo:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-unanswered-echo:a: 4.2: an 0800 touches no account and an unanswered echo needs no clean-up, so there is nothing to reverse.
recorded.prompt:q-unanswered-echo:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-unanswered-echo:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-unanswered-echo:b: 4.3 ties repeats to advices reporting something already done, and 4.2 says the next echo is a new message, not a repeat.
recorded.prompt:q-unanswered-echo:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-unanswered-echo:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-unanswered-echo:d: 4.1: function digit 1 is the response to a request, so an 0810 exists only as the answer to an 0800 (the page refutes this by definition; it does not explicitly say a host never sends an unsolicited 0810).
